n450f00048a9.s: Containers such as Docker are lighter than virtual machines mainly because they:
o: Each carry a full operating system
n450f00048a9.x: Containers share the host OS kernel, while each virtual machine runs its own operating system; this makes containers lightweight.

n8e4c9f62db7.s: The Vizag–Kapuluppada data-centre corridor lies in which seismic zone?
n8e4c9f62db7.x: Location in Seismic Zone II is one of the corridor's advantages, along with a submarine cable landing station, sea-breeze cooling and nearness to Southeast Asia.

n0bd8e045de0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Web 3.0 terms?
o: Stablecoins are pegged to fiat currencies, commodities or crypto-assets
Tokenisation means mining new coins to validate transactions
Tokenisation converts ownership rights in an asset into a blockchain token
n0bd8e045de0.x: Tokenisation converts asset ownership rights into a blockchain token; it is mining, not tokenisation, that validates transactions.

n188d19dc222.s: The property-registration pilot of MeitY's Distributed Centre of Excellence in Blockchain was in Shamshabad, which lies in:
n188d19dc222.x: Shamshabad is in Telangana, not Andhra Pradesh.

n4e43b300b5c.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n4e43b300b5c.x: Cryptocurrency is decentralised and peer-to-peer; it is not legal tender in India and has no issuer, unlike the RBI's e-rupee.

n3c6721ce1b2.s: The Bharat 6G Vision (March 2023) aims for India to lead 6G design, development and deployment by:
n3c6721ce1b2.x: The Bharat 6G Vision, released in March 2023, targets Indian leadership in 6G by 2030.

n1503deb6b9e.s: 5G Standalone (SA) gives lower latency mainly because it:
o: Splits the network into virtual slices
n1503deb6b9e.x: 5G SA runs without a 4G core, which gives it lower latency; network slicing is a separate feature and does not explain it.

n5f6140aecae.s: Under GMPCS licence conditions, what must satellite operators get made in India within five years?
n5f6140aecae.x: The GMPCS conditions require terminals to be made in India within five years, besides geofencing, no cross-border spillover and lawful surveillance.

nb48f6956a04.s: Under ITU rules, a satellite must be de-orbited within how many years of the end of its mission?
nb48f6956a04.x: The ITU de-orbit limit is 25 years after mission end; orbital slots are given first-come, first-served.

new.s: Raw data stored in its native format is called a:
new.x: A data lake holds raw data in native format; a data warehouse holds cleaned, structured data.

new.s: 'Data about data' is known as:
new.x: Metadata is data about data; data mining is finding patterns in large datasets.

new.s: Finding patterns in large datasets is called:
new.x: Data mining means finding patterns in large datasets.

new.s: Google App Engine is an example of which cloud service model?
new.x: Google App Engine is PaaS, a platform to develop, deploy and run apps; Amazon EC2 is IaaS and Gmail is SaaS.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a deployment model of cloud computing?
new.x: The deployment models are public, private, hybrid and community; 'platform' refers to the PaaS service model, not a deployment model.

new.s: The cloud feature under which many users share a common set of resources is:
new.x: Resource pooling means shared resources; elasticity means resources grow or shrink with demand.

new.s: In which model does the provider run and scale the servers and bill the user per use, as in AWS Lambda?
new.x: Serverless computing lets the provider run and scale servers with billing per use; AWS Lambda is an example.

new.s: Running many virtual machines, each with its own OS, on one server is called:
new.x: Virtualisation lets one server run many VMs, each with its own OS; containers instead share the host kernel.

new.s: Which computing layer sits between edge and cloud and does local aggregation of data?
new.x: Fog computing lies between edge and cloud and aggregates data locally; edge has the lowest latency.

new.s: The National Data Governance Framework Policy (2022) set up the India Data Management Office and the:
new.x: The NDGF Policy (MeitY, 2022) set up the India Data Management Office and the India Datasets Programme.

new.s: The Open Government Data (OGD) Platform India was set up under the NDSAP of:
new.x: The OGD Platform India comes under the NDSAP of 2012 and offers over 2.34 lakh dataset APIs.

new.s: MeghRaj (GI Cloud), the Government of India cloud, runs on the infrastructure of:
new.x: MeghRaj (GI Cloud) is the GoI cloud on NIC, with interoperability and security standards.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey 2025-26 proposal on health hotspots:
1. It uses UDISE+, AISHE and ABDM surveys.
2. It combines these surveys with AI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the Economic Survey 2025-26 proposes UDISE+, AISHE and ABDM surveys plus AI to find health hotspots.

new.s: The draft Data Centre Policy (September 2025) proposes a tax holiday of:
new.x: The draft policy proposes a 20-year tax holiday, not 10 years.

new.s: Which value of Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) shows the most efficient data centre?
new.x: PUE is total facility energy divided by IT energy; the closer to 1, the better.

new.s: The Uptime Institute Tier IV data centre offers availability of about:
new.x: Tier IV is fully fault-tolerant with about 99.995% availability; Tier I is basic.

new.s: Data centres use about what share of global electricity?
new.x: Data centres use about 1% of global electricity, and their cooling needs much water.

new.s: Which company announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI hub in Visakhapatnam in October 2025?
new.x: Google announced the $15 billion, 1 GW AI hub in Visakhapatnam in October 2025.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (investor in Visakhapatnam – project) is correctly matched?
new.x: HyperVault is TCS's data-centre proposal; the $15 billion 1 GW AI hub is Google's.

new.s: AP DigiVerify, used for certificate verification, runs on which type of blockchain?
new.x: AP DigiVerify is a permissioned blockchain where only authorised entities join and validate; Bitcoin is public and permissionless.

new.s: Which consensus mechanism uses far more energy, with miners racing to solve puzzles?
new.x: Proof of Work has miners racing to solve puzzles and uses far more energy; Proof of Stake picks validators by coins staked.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Bitcoin still uses Proof of Work
Ethereum uses Proof of Stake since September 2022
AP DigiVerify is a permissionless blockchain
new.x: AP DigiVerify is permissioned: only authorised entities join and validate.

new.s: The tax on gains from virtual digital assets under Section 115BBH is:
new.x: The Finance Act 2022 levies 30% tax on VDA gains (Section 115BBH) and 1% TDS on transfers (Section 194S).

new.s: 1% TDS on transfers of virtual digital assets is levied under which section of the Income Tax Act?
new.x: Section 194S levies 1% TDS on VDA transfers from 1 July 2022; Section 115BBH taxes the gains at 30%.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the taxation of virtual digital assets in India:
1. Gains are taxed at 30%.
2. Losses can be set off against other income.
3. 1% TDS applies on transfers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; losses on VDAs cannot be set off.

new.s: Lending and trading through smart contracts without banks is called:
new.x: DeFi (decentralised finance) means lending and trading via smart contracts without banks.

new.s: NFTs are called non-fungible because they:
o: Are issued only by central banks
Cannot be held as digital assets
Are unique and not exchangeable at equivalency
new.x: NFTs are unique tokens not exchangeable at equivalency; they can even represent physical assets.

new.s: Vishvasya, MeitY's 2024 blockchain stack, is offered as:
new.x: Vishvasya is a Blockchain-as-a-Service stack across NIC data centres, building on the National Blockchain Framework.

new.s: The Vishvasya blockchain stack is hosted across the data centres of:
new.x: Vishvasya (MeitY, 2024) runs across NIC data centres.

new.s: Which blockchain did NPCI release as its first, before Drunix?
new.x: Falcon was NPCI's first open-source blockchain; Drunix, rebuilt from Hyperledger Fabric, is the second.

new.s: The Distributed Centre of Excellence in Blockchain produced a Proof-of-Existence framework for:
new.x: The Distributed CoE (C-DAC, IDRBT Hyderabad, VJTI Mumbai) produced a Proof-of-Existence framework for certificates.

new.s: On 1 January 2026, the Supreme Court suggested the use of blockchain for:
new.x: On 1 January 2026 the Supreme Court suggested blockchain for land records.

new.s: India's CBDC, the e-rupee, is issued by the:
new.x: The e-rupee is legal tender in digital form issued by the RBI and is a liability of the RBI.

new.s: The wholesale e-rupee (e₹-W) pilot began on:
new.x: The wholesale pilot began on 1 November 2022, before the retail pilot of 1 December 2022.

new.s: The wholesale e-rupee pilot is used for the settlement of:
new.x: The wholesale pilot (e₹-W) settles secondary-market government securities, with 9 banks.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the e-rupee:
1. It is legal tender.
2. Like UPI, it only moves bank-account money.
3. The retail pilot began on 1 December 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; UPI moves bank-account money, whereas the e-rupee is RBI money itself.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: UPI – RBI money in digital form
new.x: The e-rupee is a liability of the RBI (concept note, October 2022); UPI moves bank-account money and crypto has no issuer and is not legal tender.

new.s: The Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot unifies which three AP departments?
new.x: Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain, launched by CM Naidu on 23 July 2026, unifies Revenue, Survey and Registration.

new.s: The Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot was launched by Chief Minister Naidu on:
new.x: The pilot was launched on 23 July 2026 and is to go statewide from November.

new.s: Which body is DoT's technical arm for telecom standards and equipment testing?
new.x: TEC is DoT's technical body for standards and equipment testing (not USOF collection); C-DOT is the R&D centre.

new.s: India launched 5G services on 1 October 2022 at the:
new.x: India's 5G launch was on 1 October 2022 at the India Mobile Congress.

new.s: MTNL and VSNL were set up in:
new.x: MTNL and VSNL came in 1986, after C-DOT (1984) and DoT (1985); TRAI came in 1997.

new.s: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) was set up in:
new.x: TRAI was set up in 1997; TDSAT came through the 2000 amendment.

new.s: 3G mobile technology is based on:
new.x: 3G is CDMA-based (WCDMA/CDMA2000); 4G and 5G use OFDMA and 1G was analog FDMA.

new.s: WLL, the radio link that replaces the copper last mile, stands for:
new.x: WLL is Wireless Local Loop, a radio link replacing the copper last mile.

new.s: 5G offers latency as low as about:
new.x: 5G uses OFDMA and offers latency as low as 1 ms.

new.s: Which 5G band gives very high data rates but only a short range?
new.x: mmWave gives very high data rates over short range; sub-6 GHz (low/mid) gives wider coverage and better penetration.

new.s: The Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF) receives what share of the Digital Bharat Nidhi?
new.x: TTDF (2022) gets 5% of the Digital Bharat Nidhi, about Rs 500 crore a year.

new.s: The Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) was launched in:
new.x: The Bharat 6G Alliance was launched in 2023 and has seven Working Groups.

new.s: 6G is expected to arrive in the:
new.x: 6G is expected in the early 2030s and is described as 'omnipresent wireless intelligence'.

new.s: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced telecom licensing with:
new.x: The Telecommunications Act 2023 moved from licensing to authorisation.

new.s: In February 2026, TRAI recommended cutting the net-worth requirement for a new entrant per service area from Rs 100 crore to:
new.x: TRAI (February 2026) recommended a cut from Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore per service area.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about spectrum under the Telecommunications Act, 2023:
1. Terrestrial spectrum is auctioned.
2. Satellite spectrum is auctioned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only statement 1 is correct; under the First Schedule satellite spectrum is assigned administratively, not auctioned.

new.s: Which of the following satellite series operates in geostationary orbit?
new.x: GSAT satellites are GEO; Starlink, OneWeb and Kuiper are LEO constellations.

new.s: LEO satellites orbit Earth at altitudes below about:
new.x: LEO satellites are below about 2,000 km and have low latency; GEO satellites are at about 35,786 km.

new.s: The CANI undersea optical fibre cable links Chennai with:
new.x: CANI (Chennai–Andaman and Nicobar Islands), about 2,300 km, was inaugurated on 10 August 2020.

new.s: The National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN) is funded by the:
new.x: NOFN, covering 2,50,000 Gram Panchayats, is funded by USOF, not NIIF.

new.s: Which type of optical fibre is used for long distances?
new.x: Single-mode fibre is used for long distances; multi-mode for short runs.

new.s: Which of the following has the highest refractive index?
new.x: Refractive index order is Diamond > Glass > Water > Air.

new.s: Google's Project Loon used which of the following to provide internet?
new.x: Project Loon (Google/Alphabet) used stratospheric helium balloons for internet and was shut in January 2021.

new.s: Wi-Fi 6 corresponds to the IEEE standard:
new.x: Wi-Fi 6 is 802.11ax; Wi-Fi 7 is 802.11be and WiMAX is 802.16.

new.s: Transmitting data by laser beams through the air without fibre is called:
new.x: FSO (free-space optics) sends data by laser beams without fibre.

new.s: According to PM Gati Shakti NMP data (2026), the number of PM-WANI hotspots is about:
new.x: PM Gati Shakti NMP (2026) shows about 3.15 lakh PM-WANI hotspots, 8.26 lakh towers and 13.5 lakh route km of OFC.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Li-Fi?
o: It uses visible light from LEDs
It offers more bandwidth than Wi-Fi
Its term was coined by Harald Haas
new.x: Li-Fi does not pass through walls; Wi-Fi, which uses radio waves, does.

new.s: Radio tags read wirelessly, as used in Kavach track tags, are an example of:
new.x: RFID uses radio tags read wirelessly, such as Kavach track tags.
